conviction_note: The equity is a roughly $26m stub (35.4m shares at $0.74) on top of about $122m of bank debt and a $26.5m earnout due April 2027, so a small change in EBITDA moves it a long way. The evidence leans to a Q3 marketing shortfall and a fourth guidance cut in a row: Catena's Q3 was -29% on generative search, the company's own Q2 had casino -22% and marketing -10%, and the H2 guide needs a steep ramp. Against that, the stock is already -42% in 20 days and -59% since the reaffirm, the last 'no cut' print bought +19%, and Better Collective's Q3 North America (+28%) supports the non-SEO two-thirds of revenue. So p_up is 44, not lower. abs_move is 25 from the name's own last prints (-38% on the May cut, +19% on the August reaffirm). The findings sum to -2.8 and the scaled number is -3.0, so the two measurements agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus about $41.5m and EPS $0.05 (Earnings Whispers, https://finviz.com/news/421348/grandstand-must-prove-a-swing-to-profit-is-real-after-a-59-collapse, 2026-11-11); FXEmpire has $41.99m and EPS $0.04 (https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/grsd/earnings). Two sources, within about 1%. FY2026 consensus revenue is $165.4m, at or just below the low end of the company's $165-170m guide (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/grsd/forecast/, 8 analysts, targets last updated 2026-08-14 and stale: average $4.43 against a $0.74 spot). Company guide: FY revenue $165-170m, adj. EBITDA $45-50m, with sequential growth in both revenue and adj. EBITDA through H2 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001839799/000183979926000138/gamb-q22026xpressrelease.htm). The $0.74 price says the market's real bar sits far below the sell-side numbers.
positioning_check: Short interest about 1.1M shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, 6.7 days to cover on about 163k shares a day (https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/GRSD/short-interest). That is about 3.1% of roughly 35.4m shares (count implied by the Q2 net loss of $4.6m at $0.13/share), higher as a share of the free float. At 2026-10-15 it was 0.97M shares and 5.2 days, so shorts were building modestly into the print. Not crowded. No usable option chain (ATM legs not two-sided), so there is no skew; put/call open interest is 0.03 on 4,092 contracts, almost all calls. Tape: -8.8% over 5 days, -42.1% over 20 days, -87.1% from the 52-week high, 2.0% above the 52-week low, 20-day realised vol 87%.

findings.finding: Catena Media, a search-led gambling affiliate, pre-released Q3 2026 on 2026-10-16: revenue EUR 8.3m, -29% YoY; adj. EBITDA EUR 0.7m against 2.9m; a EUR 30-35m impairment; its 2026 growth target dropped. It blamed generative/AI search taking new traffic from the whole affiliate industry, lower traditional rankings, and operators cutting budgets over the summer. Grandstand's own SEO business (about one third of revenue per its Q2 call) was already falling: Q2 casino revenue was -22% and marketing -10% YoY. Management's plan needs H2 marketing roughly flat YoY, i.e. Q3 marketing near the $29.8m of Q3 2025, against $26.5m in Q2 2026. If marketing repeats Q2's -10% YoY (about $26.8m) and data reaches about $11.7m, Q3 revenue is about $38.5m against a $41.5-42.0m consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SEO-driven marketing misses led to the Q3 2025 guide cut (stock plunged, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1839799/000183979925000075/gamb-q32025xpressrelease.htm cites weak organic search) and to the Q1 2026 guide cut (-38% intraday, https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/gamb-stock-hits-record-lows-earnings-guidance-cut-layoffs/cZXl64rRejF). An in-line Q2 with a reaffirm bought +19% (https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/grsd/earnings).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: GRSD fell about 28% in October after this release and is down 42% over 20 days. But the sell-side Q3 revenue estimate ($41.5-42.0m, +6-8% YoY, +10-11% QoQ) has not moved down to what an affiliate-wide search collapse implies. If it had, consensus would sit near or below Q3 2025's $39.0m. This is a proxy: Catena is far more SEO- and CPA-dependent (over 90% CPA) than Grandstand, whose non-SEO two thirds grew in North America (+63% in Q2).
findings.independence: Same direction, different sources: Google's May 2026 core update (rolled out 2026-05-21 to 06-02) hit iGaming sites hard (https://www.gsqi.com/marketing-blog/core-roars-back-google-may-2026-core-update-analysis/), so Q3 is its first full quarter. Grandstand's own Q2 release (casino -22%, marketing -10%) is a separate primary document. Raketech's Q3 (affiliation -14%, https://affpapa.com/raketech-q3-2026-revenue-falls-to-e5m/) is weaker support, since it is driven by a planned wind-down. Net of the rest of the company: data (+12% in Q2, about $11-12m a quarter) and North American marketing have to offset SEO; finding 4 below supports that side.

findings.finding: The reaffirmed FY2026 guide ($165-170m revenue, $45-50m adj. EBITDA; H1 actual $78.2m revenue and $16.7m adj. EBITDA) requires H2 revenue of $86.8-91.8m and H2 adj. EBITDA of $28.3-33.3m. That means Q4 alone would need about $45-50m of revenue and about $16-20m of EBITDA against a record Q4 2025 of $46.2m and $15.5m. On the Q2 call management said reaching the top of the range needs an SEO recovery, and the FY revenue consensus ($165.4m) already sits at the bottom. Missing it would be the company's fourth consecutive guidance cut, after Q3 2025, the March 2026 initial guide and the May 2026 cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide cut, May 2026: about -25% after hours and -38% intraday the next day. Weak initial 2026 guide, March 2026: price-target cuts and a fall (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/gambling-com-group-limited-gamb-000841410.html). Guide cut, Nov 2025: plunge. Reaffirm, Aug 2026: +19%. This stock moves 20-40% on the guide line in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: The price has largely priced a cut: a ~$26m market cap against EV/guide-EBITDA of about 3.5x is a distressed valuation. The sell-side has not (FY consensus at the guide's low end, targets $3-6). What is not knowable from the price is the size of the cut, and that decides whether this is -20% or +20%. A cut to EBITDA in the low $40m range could be read as relief at this price; a cut into the $30m range would bring finding 3 into play.
findings.independence: Q2 call commentary (https://www.webull.ca/news-detail/15401380805108736): H2 marketing roughly flat, top of range needs SEO recovery. That is the same company, a different document. Finding 1 is the external pressure on the same line and shares its arithmetic only partly.

findings.finding: Covenant headroom is thin going into Q3 and its disclosure lands with this print. The amended Wells Fargo facility requires maximum leverage of 3.00x, a minimum fixed-charge ratio of 1.25x and minimum liquidity of $15.0m (FY2025 20-F). At 2026-06-30 borrowings were $122.3m, cash $8.8m, total liquidity $33.3m, net current liabilities $23.1m, and $26.5m of OddsJam deferred consideration was current (payable April 2027). Trailing adj. EBITDA at Q2 was about $45.2m (FY25 $58.0m - H1'25 $29.5m + H1'26 $16.7m), about 2.7x gross. In Q3 the $13.0m of Q3 2025 EBITDA rolls off, so a Q3 2026 adj. EBITDA below about $8.6m would put gross debt/TTM EBITDA above 3.0x (the covenant's exact debt definition is not public in what I read). Separately, paying the $26.5m earnout in cash would take liquidity below the $15m minimum unless the facility is amended or part of it is paid in shares; the 6-K says up to 70% of the 2026 amount may be settled in ordinary shares, which at $0.74 would be heavily dilutive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on record: covenants have not been discussed on a call (the Q2 call did not cover covenant terms) and no amendment has been filed in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: a $26m equity value on $122m of debt is the market pricing exactly this risk. What is not priced is the outcome: an amendment or refinancing announced with the print would be relief, while a waiver, a going-concern note or a share-settled earnout would be another leg down. Financing question answered: the money funds an acquisition earnout (OddsJam, the growing data segment) and existing debt service, not new demand, so the sign is negative but small, because it can resolve either way.
findings.independence: Uses the same 6-K as finding 2 for the H1 numbers. The covenant levels come from a different document, the 20-F. No outside source confirms covenant stress; the company stated 'no material uncertainty' on going concern at 2026-06-30.

findings.finding: Better Collective, the largest listed peer, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-18 after Grandstand last spoke: record Q3 revenue, +6% organic; EBITDA before special items +6% at a 26% margin; North America +28% at a 39% margin; publishing +16%, with prediction markets cited as a driver; full-year guidance unchanged. Low sports win margins cost it about EUR 6.5m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No GRSD-specific record of reacting to peer prints. GRSD's North American marketing grew +63% in Q2 and is the part management says carries the H2 ramp.
findings.why_not_priced: Published the evening before GRSD's print and in Copenhagen, so GRSD's US holder base has had one session to read it, and the GRSD tape (-8.8% over 5 days) shows no read-through rally. It points against the 'all affiliates collapse' reading that Catena created. The low sports win margin it cites hurts revenue-share income, which is about 50% of GRSD revenue counting subscriptions.
findings.independence: DraftKings Q3 2026 (finding 5, https://www.covers.com/industry/draftkings-sports-predictions-success-fuels-q3-revenue-growth-nov-5-2026) is a different counterparty showing US sports strength. Partly offset by Catena (finding 1).

findings.finding: DraftKings, a direct US customer of affiliates, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-05: sports net revenue margin 5.6% against 5.2% a year earlier, sports revenue +31.5%, combined sportsbook and predictions volume +22%. But US iGaming (online casino) grew only +2.1%, and DraftKings is spending $650-700m in FY2026 on prediction markets, much of it customer acquisition. For Grandstand that means US sports revenue share and CPA demand are firm, while the casino vertical (Q3 2025: $23.2m, 59% of revenue) gets little help.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No GRSD record. Grandstand's Q2 sports vertical grew +17% and the Q2 call said prediction markets are 'adding marketing demand'.
findings.why_not_priced: Customer-to-affiliate transmission is not confirmed by Grandstand. DraftKings itself fell 23% on its guide, so sector sentiment was negative, and GRSD kept falling after Nov 5. Small because it is a proxy.
findings.independence: Better Collective's North America +28% (finding 4) is a different source pointing the same way for the US sports side.

findings.finding: Restructuring: the May 2026 plan (25% headcount cut, $13m annualised savings) is substantially complete, with about $6.5m of fixed-cost savings expected in H2 2026 starting in Q3. That supports margin expansion on the adj. EBITDA line even if Q3 revenue misses: about $3m+ a quarter against Q2's $7.7m adj. EBITDA.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The savings were announced with the May guide cut (-38%), so they were not paid for then.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside what the company has guided, so it is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect; sized near zero. It matters because it decides whether Q3 adj. EBITDA clears the roughly $8.6m level in finding 3.
findings.independence: The same 6-K as findings 2 and 3; it counts once.

findings.finding: Price versus last reaction: at $0.74 the stock is -59% since the 2026-08-13 print (post-print range $2.41 high, $0.81 low before this week) and -42% over 20 days. No company filing since August explains the slide; the October 6-K record is empty apart from a Form 4. The last print that avoided a guide cut bought +19% from $1.91.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: +19.4% on the Q2 2026 reaffirm (https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/grsd/earnings); -38% on the Q1 2026 cut.
findings.why_not_priced: This is about positioning, not information. The drawdown has partial causes (finding 1, the DraftKings sell-off), so it is not cleanly an over-reaction. Sized small; the asymmetry it creates is carried in abs_move_pct, not here.
findings.independence: Short interest is building modestly (0.97M to 1.1M shares, https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/GRSD/short-interest) but is not crowded.

findings.finding: The CEO, Kevin McCrystle, bought 2,901 shares in the open market at $1.16 on 2026-10-15 (Form 4 filed 2026-10-19), taking his direct holding to 1,004,786 shares. It is the only insider transaction since August.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a month and token in size (about $3.4k), so close to zero. It says the CEO was not in a blackout and chose to buy two weeks after quarter-end, a weak hint that Q3 was not a disaster in his eyes.

outside_window.finding: OddsJam deferred consideration of $26.5m is payable around April 2027, against $33.3m of liquidity and a $15m minimum-liquidity covenant; Spotlight.Vegas earnouts of up to $11m are payable in April 2027 and April 2028. How these are funded (cash, revolver, up to 70% in shares) settles after the window unless the company announces it with the print. That part is covered in finding 3.

Nasdaq minimum bid price: the stock has traded below $1.00 since about early November 2026 (around $1.05 at the start of November, $0.83 on 11-13). A deficiency notice needs 30 consecutive business days below $1, which lands around mid-to-late December, followed by a 180-day cure period.

baseline_tension: The evidence agrees with the tape: the -42% in 20 days and the 52-week low are the market already pricing the search damage and the guide cut. That is why the negative lean is held to p_up 44 rather than the 35-40 the company-level numbers alone would support, and there is no skew to argue against.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (proxy smaller; net of the rest of the company, rule 9): Catena read-through cut from -3.0 to -2.0, since Grandstand's non-SEO two thirds and North America (+63%) offset SEO

'None was reasoning from covenant arithmetic' and rule 4 (financing is a question): covenant-headroom finding cut from -2.0 to -1.0; the sign stays negative because the money funds an earnout and debt service, not a demand ramp
Rule 1 (a fact is not a reaction) plus the name's both-ways reaction on the guide line: guidance-cut finding cut from -3.0 to -2.5
Rule 6 (inside what was guided): restructuring savings cut from +0.5 to +0.3
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0, positioning does not file large): price-versus-last-reaction finding cut from +1.0 to +0.5

'A peer's print landing after the company last spoke' is the pattern that has paid: Better Collective kept positive but trimmed from +1.5 to +1.2, because it is Europe-weighted and reported a low sports win margin
Rule 3 (a caveat moves p_up toward 50): p_up moved from 42 to 44, abs_move held at 25 (rule 8, understatement), so expected_move went from -4.0 to -3.0
